'''Kyrylo Anatoliyovych Fesenko''' ({{langx|uk|Кирило Анатолійович Фесенко}}; born 24 December 1986) is a Ukrainian former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Al-Nasr SC (Benghazi, basketball)|Al-Nasr SC]] of the [[Libyan Division I Basketball League]]. Standing at {{height|m=2.16}}, he plays the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. He wears a size 18 shoe and has a {{height|ft=7|in=4}} wingspan and {{height|ft=9|in=4}} standing reach (same standing reach as [[Greg Oden]]).<ref name="2007 bio" />

==Basketball career==

===Early career (2003–2006)===
Born in [[Dnipropetrovsk]], Fesenko began his basketball career in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]], first with the second division team of [[BC Azovmash]] in 2003 then to its first division from 2004 to 2006. He then played for the [[Cherkaski Mavpy]] for a season.<ref name="2007 bio">{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kyrylo_fesenko/bio.html |title=Kyrylo Fesenko |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090302025503/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/kyrylo_fesenko/bio.html |archive-date=2009-03-02 }}</ref>

===First NBA stint (2007–2013)===
After playing four seasons in native Ukraine, Fesenko was selected 38th overall in the second round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] and then traded to the [[Utah Jazz]], signing a three-year contract with the Jazz on 15 August, 2007.<ref>{{cite news|first=Linda |last=Hamilton |title=Sleepless Fesenko inks Jazz contract |url=http://deseretnews.com/article/1%2C5143%2C695201246%2C00.html |work=[[Deseret Morning News]] |date=August 16, 2007 |access-date=January 15, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071211235448/http://deseretnews.com/article/1%2C5143%2C695201246%2C00.html |archive-date=December 11, 2007 }}</ref> In 2010, he turned down a multiyear deal with the Houston Rockets and re-signed with the Jazz for 1 year. He became an unrestricted free agent in 2011.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5620481 |title=Sources: Kyrylo Fesenko back to Jazz |author=Marc Stein |work=[[ESPN.com]] |date=September 27, 2010 |access-date=November 17, 2010 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100930162457/http://sports.espn.go.com/nba/news/story?id=5620481 |archive-date=September 30, 2010 }}</ref> He spent most of his rookie season with the [[NBA Development League]] [[Utah Flash]].

On 30 November 2007, Fesenko made his NBA debut against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. He was recalled from the [[Utah Flash]] due to the absence of [[Carlos Boozer]] (sprained ankle) and [[Mehmet Okur]] (back spasms). Fesenko scored 6 points, had 7 rebounds and managed 1 assist.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20071130/LALUTA/boxscore.html |title=Lakers at Jazz Game Info |date=November 30, 2007 |work=NBA.com |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090306113737/http://www.nba.com/games/20071130/LALUTA/boxscore.html |archive-date=March 6, 2009 }}</ref>

Fesenko spent part of the [[2011–12 NBA season]] with the [[Indiana Pacers]]. In October 2012, he joined the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11036 |title=Bulls add Ryan Allen, Vance Cooksey, Andre Emmett, Kyrylo Fesenko, Marko Jaric to training camp |publisher=Inside Hoops |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131004214249/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11036 |archive-date=2013-10-04 }}</ref> Later that month he was waived.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11201 |title=Bulls waive center Kyrylo Fesenko |publisher=Inside Hoops |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121020042255/http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=11201 |archive-date=2012-10-20 }}</ref>

===Return to Europe (2013)===
In January 2013, Fesenko signed with [[BC Donetsk]].<ref>{{cite web|title=BC Donetsk announced Kyrylo Fesenko |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/48803/bc-donetsk-announced-kyrylo-fesenko.html |publisher=Sportando.net |date=April 1, 2013 |access-date=May 2, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110115345/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/ukraine/48803/bc-donetsk-announced-kyrylo-fesenko.html |archive-date=January 10, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> In November 2013, he signed with [[Śląsk Wrocław (basketball)|Śląsk Wrocław]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Fesenko signs with Slask Wroclaw |url=http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/poland/66979/fesenko-signs-with-slask-wroclaw.html |date=August 11, 2013 |access-date=November 8, 2013 |newspaper=Sportando.net |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140110115727/http://www.sportando.net/eng/europe/poland/66979/fesenko-signs-with-slask-wroclaw.html |archive-date=January 10, 2014 |url-status=live }}</ref> He later left Wrocław before appearing in a game for them.

===D-League / Return to NBA (2014)===
In January 2014, Fesenko was acquired by the [[Delaware 87ers]]. On March 8, 2014, he was traded to the [[Canton Charge]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_acquire_buford_fesenko_2014_03_08.html |title=Charge Acquire Buford, Fesenko |work=NBA.com |access-date=March 9, 2014 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140312083345/http://www.nba.com/dleague/canton/news/charge_acquire_buford_fesenko_2014_03_08.html |archive-date=March 12, 2014 }}</ref>

On 18 September 2014, Fesenko signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/timberwolves-sign-kyrylo-fesenko-and-brady-heslip Timberwolves Sign Kyrylo Fesenko and Brady Heslip]</ref> However, he was later waived by the Timberwolves on October 20, 2014.<ref>{{cite news|title=Timberwolves Waive Kyrylo Fesenko|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-kyrylo-fesenko|access-date=October 20, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2014}}</ref>

===Return to Europe (2014–2021)===
On 5 November 2014, Fesenko signed with the [[VTB United League]] and [[EuroChallenge]] team [[Avtodor Saratov]].<ref>[http://www.fibaeurope.com/eurochallenge/cid_04nV5LW1InMnPsDwhkujE0.pageID_ryF4e9o2IbYrbd4ZRqn7g0.compID_BYg5Rb55Jw-G5I3MZ6JB01.season_2015.coid_5VkG5ncLJQMz5wDjgc4Rr0.articleMode_on.html Avtodor Bring In Big Man Fesenko]</ref>

On 9 June 2015, Fesenko signed a one-year contract with [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Kyrylo Fesenko joined Loko|url=http://en.lokobasket.com/news/4881391.html|access-date=9 June 2015|work=lokobasket.com|date=9 June 2015}}{{Dead link|date=February 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> On January 5, 2016, he parted ways with Lokomotiv,<ref>{{cite news|title=Кирилл Фесенко уходит из "Локо", Никита Зверев отправляется в аренду|url=http://lokobasket.com/news/5310097.html|access-date=5 January 2016|work=lokobasket.com|date=5 January 2016|language=ru}}</ref> and the following day he was hired until the end of the season by [[Pallacanestro Cantù]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.pallacanestrocantu.com/news.html?id=5590|title=LA PALLACANESTRO CANTU' INGAGGIA KYRYLO FESENKO|language=it|publisher=[[Pallacanestro Cantù]]|date=2016-01-06|access-date=2016-01-06}}</ref> On May 6, 2016, he left Cantù and signed with [[AS Monaco Basket]] for the rest of the [[2015–16 LNB Pro A season]].<ref>[http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/france/198862/as-monaco-lands-kyrylo-fesenko.html AS Monaco lands Kyrylo Fesenko]</ref>

On 16 August 2016, Fesenko signed with Italian club [[S.S. Felice Scandone|Sidigas Avellino]] for the 2016–17 season.<ref>[http://www.eurohoops.net/fiba/300240/avellino-signed-kyrylo-fesenko Avellino signed Kyrylo Fesenko]</ref> On July 30, 2017, he re-signed with Avellino for one more season.<ref>[https://www.sportando.com/en/italy/serie-a/242866/kyrylo-fesenko-re-sign-with-avellino.html Kyrylo Fesenko re-sign with Avellino]</ref>

===Iran (2021–present)===
In October 2021, Fesenko signed with [[Sanaye Hormozgan BC| Sanaye Hormozgan]] of the [[Iranian Basketball Super League]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Former leader of the national team of Ukraine and Dnipro will continue his career in Iran |url=https://thetimeshub.in/former-leader-of-the-national-team-of-ukraine-and-dnipro-will-continue-his-career-in-iran |access-date=11 December 2021 |work=The Times Hub |date=19 October 2021}}</ref>
